relevance.rationale: *** WRONG JOIN ***. The seeded id points at a single-author general-relativity textbook. The document is a two-author research preprint on observables in loop quantum gravity with a cosmological constant (arXiv:1311.6841v1). Type, authorship and date all differ; id set to null (greps for '1311.6841' and for both author surnames in references.ts are empty). CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SEEDED KEY: wald1984 is cited at QOU/QuantumObservableUniverse/GaugeTheory.lean:197 (theorem variational_einstein) and QOU/MathlibExt/MonoidalCalcVar.lean:41 and :109, the latter with a numbered-theorem locator and a section locator for the Einstein equation. Those uses are prima facie appropriate for a GR textbook, but no copy of that textbook exists in uploads/, so the locators are unverified and this upload does not supply them. On merits the actual document is relevant to the folio: it introduces U_q(su(2)) spin networks into loop quantum gravity, builds tensor operators and a quantum-group U_q(u(n)) analogue of the U(N) formalism, and constructs length, area and angle observables that characterise a quantum discrete HYPERBOLIC geometry - an independent line in which q-deformation encodes a cosmological constant and yields hyperbolic geometric observables, structurally parallel to the folio's q-substrate and its hyperbolic-volume observables.

keyResults.statement: U_q(su(2)) tensor operators give length, area and angle observables whose spectra characterise a quantum discrete HYPERBOLIC geometry in 3d LQG, with q-deformation encoding a non-zero cosmological constant.
keyResults.useForFolio: An independent (non-QOU) instance of 'q-deformation of the gauge structure produces hyperbolic geometric observables' - useful as external context for the corpus's q-substrate-to-hyperbolic-volume step, and as a comparison case in the observations chapter.

proposedActions.rationale: Corpus-relevant document with no ref() entry, currently mis-joined onto the [wald1984] entry. Register from its title page.

The observations chapter already compares QOU against parallel unification programmes (causal fermion systems). A q-deformed-LQG comparison entry is the same kind of external-context remark and this document is the source for it.
